title: Seeded application maintenance corpus
description: Cross-language comparison of agents modifying four existing hidden-correct programs to satisfy new application requirements.

matrix.derivation: 6 complete four-task maintenance bundles x 3 languages

primary_gate.correctness: Parley hidden-task success must be 100% and no lower than either baseline.
primary_gate.tokens: Parley median reported total tokens per assigned task must be no higher than the lower Python/Rust median.
primary_gate.elapsed: Parley median elapsed seconds per assigned task must be no higher than the lower Python/Rust median.
primary_gate.first_check: Parley first-check task success rate must be no lower than the higher Python/Rust rate.
primary_gate.verdict: All four conditions must hold for strict maintenance-corpus parity.

interpretation_boundary: The primary result is the within-iteration Parley/Python/Rust comparison under gpt-5.6-sol.
The four requirement extensions and their public/hidden cases are new, but the seed programs are preserved hidden-correct outputs from iteration 023.
This related-source design measures maintenance work and cannot count as independent language-feature recurrence.
Every agent receives the exact starting source in its measured prompt and workspace; final and seed source sizes plus deterministic rough-token edit counts are recorded.
Cross-iteration movement is descriptive only because the unit of work changed from cold-start generation to seeded maintenance.
secondary_analysis: Report every session, task outcome, repair, token count, elapsed time, prompt size, seed/final source size, edit size, integrity result, and command-protocol result.
Classify every first-check and hidden failure by maintenance family and independent session.
Compare Parley seed, final, and edit size with Python and Rust to test whether compact source materially helps maintenance.
Report repair-free sensitivity if at least two Parley sessions pass all four tasks on the first check.
feature_boundary: Parley remains frozen at v0.3.155 with the exact 1,519-character skill. Only the language-neutral benchmark harness gained optional seed-source presentation and edit-size measurement; cold-start behavior remains backward compatible.
change_rule: No syntax, compiler, grammar, AST, checker, runtime, diagnostic, prompt skill, or benchmark instruction may change from iteration 024 output. This related-source corpus cannot satisfy independent recurrence. Future proposals require unrelated new tasks and independent sessions, then general usefulness, semantic consistency, and maintainability review.
instruction_rule: The proven 1,519-character skill remains byte-for-byte unchanged and is injected once per Parley session. The one allowed instruction-compression experiment is closed.
stop_rule: Preserve the complete result without selective reruns. If strict parity passes, preregister a broader real-repository confirmation before claiming general parity. If it fails, make no same-corpus language or instruction change; choose the next evidence source by external validity rather than transcript syntax.
